editorial:
Imagine being a young woman in old-fashioned France who is treated more like a science project than a person. You will meet Augustine, a girl who suffers from hysteria and becomes the favorite patient of a famous doctor named Professor Charcot. He uses her to show off his hypnosis tricks to crowds of people. The vibe is a bit heavy and strange, as you watch her struggle to find her own voice while being controlled by the men around her. It is a slow burn that focuses on the power struggle between a patient and her doctor, making you feel her frustration as she tries to break free.

The acting is the best part here because you can really feel the tension in every scene. While the movie moves slowly, it keeps you interested because you want to see if Augustine ever gains control over her life. If you like historical dramas that feel more like a psychological game, you will love this. Since the visuals are so detailed and moody, you should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV to see every detail of the old hospital. It is a great pick for a quiet night in.
endingExplained: In the end, Augustine stops being a passive patient and starts using her knowledge of hypnosis to manipulate the doctor himself. She turns the tables and makes him feel the same loss of control she felt. This shift in power shows that she is no longer a victim. She eventually leaves the hospital, finally free from the doctor's grip and the labels they put on her, winning her independence through her own wit.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas and stories about psychological power struggles.
